payload.text:
Vayu Code is a browser-based Integrated Development Environment (IDE) tailored for design software development, leveraging the Puter.js framework for seamless cloud-native features like AI code generation, web search, and real-time collaboration. It emulates the sleek, minimalist interface of z.ai with a modern blur glass (glassmorphism) theme, featuring frosted transparency, subtle gradients, and glowing accents for an immersive, futuristic coding experience. Powered by Puter.js's serverless AI and cloud capabilities, Vayu Code integrates multiple LLMs including Google Gemini, ChatGPT (via OpenAI models), Claude, DeepSeek, and others to generate, debug, and optimize code directly in the browser. ## Core Architecture Vayu Code runs entirely client-side using Puter.js (``), eliminating servers, API keys, or backend setup. The app initializes with Puter.js for authentication, storage, and AI routing—handling over 500 models transparently. Key layers include: - **Frontend Stack**: HTML5 Canvas/WebGL for design previews, Monaco Editor (VS Code's core) for code editing, and Tailwind CSS for responsive glassmorphism styling (e.g., `backdrop-blur-md bg-white/30 border border-white/20 shadow-xl`). - **Puter.js Integration**: Core for AI chats (`puter.ai.chat(prompt, {model: 'gemini-pro'})`), web search (`puter.search(query)`), file storage (`puter.fs`), and real-time sync. - **Modular AI Pipeline**: Routes prompts to models via Puter.js—e.g., Claude for reasoning-heavy tasks, DeepSeek for cost-efficient code gen, Gemini/ChatGPT for multimodal design outputs. This setup mirrors browser IDEs like StackBlitz or Theia but adds native AI without plugins. ## Interface Design (z.ai-Inspired Glassmorphism) The UI adopts z.ai's clean, card-based layout with heavy glassmorphism for depth: - **Layout**: Split-view—left sidebar (file explorer, AI chat), central Monaco editor, right panel (live design preview, code diffs). Top bar for model selector (Gemini, ChatGPT, etc.), search, and theme toggle. - **Theme Elements**: | Component | Styling Description | Purpose | |-----------|--------------------|---------| | Sidebar | `bg-gradient-to-br from-slate-900/80 to-black/50 backdrop-blur-xl border-r border-white/10` | Opaque glass for navigation; animates on hover. | | Editor Cards | `bg-white/20 backdrop-blur-2xl rounded-2xl shadow-2xl ring-1 ring-white/30` | Frosted panels for code/tabs; glows on focus. | | Chat Bubble | `bg-blue-500/30 backdrop-blur-lg border border-blue-400/50 animate-pulse` | Pulsing glass for AI responses. | | Preview Canvas | Fullscreen overlay with `bg-neutral-900/40 backdrop-blur-md` | Blurred background for design rendering. | Responsive for mobile/desktop, with dark mode default and neumorphic shadows for buttons. ## AI-Powered Coding Workflow Vayu Code's "web chat" is a persistent sidebar powered by Puter.js AI, enabling natural language coding for design software (e.g., SVG animators, UI builders). - **Code Generation**: User types "Build a responsive navbar in Tailwind with glassmorphism"—chat routes to Claude (`puter.ai.chat(prompt, {model: 'claude-3.5-sonnet'})`), generates Monaco-insertable code, and previews it live. - **Multi-Model Selector**: Dropdown switches models dynamically: - Google Gemini: Multimodal (upload sketches → HTML/CSS). - ChatGPT/o1: Step-by-step debugging. - Claude: Complex logic/architecture. - DeepSeek: Fast, cheap iterations. - Others (Grok, Llama via Puter.js): Fallback for niche tasks. - **Web Search Integration**: "Research blur glass trends" → `puter.search("glassmorphism CSS 2026 trends")`, injects snippets into chat for context-aware code. Example chat flow: ``` User: Generate React component for animated SVG wind effect. AI (Gemini): [Code block inserted] + Live preview + "Refine with DeepSeek?" ``` ## Key Features - **Design Software Focus**: Built-in Canvas API for vector editing; AI generates Three.js/WebGL shaders from prompts like "Phong-shaded 3D model." - **Real-Time Collaboration**: Puter.js FS for shared files; WebSockets via Puter for multiplayer editing. - **Extensions**: Plugin system loads npm modules client-side; AI auto-installs (e.g., "Add Framer Motion"). - **Performance**: WebContainers/WebAssembly for node-like env; Puter.js handles heavy AI off-browser. - **Monetization/Security**: Free tier via Puter.js limits; user-owned data, no backend leaks. ## Implementation Starter Code ```html
``` Deploy instantly—host on GitHub Pages. Extend with Puter.js docs for full search/FS. [itsfoss](https://itsfoss.com/puter-js-ai-without-api/)

**Defining Core Features**

I'm solidifying the core features of "Vayu Code". Integrating Puter.js is essential for AI, search, and storage. I'm prioritizing multi-model AI, including Gemini, Claude, GPT, and DeepSeek, to provide choice. Finally, I'm leaning heavily towards glassmorphism and a sleek, minimalist aesthetic for a modern feel.

use this 
To build an entire software application using Puter.js within your IDE (like VS Code, IntelliJ, or WebStorm), you don't use "modules" in the sense of separate plugins. Instead, you integrate the Puter.js NPM library into your project, which gives you access to a full suite of serverless backend services. 
Core Modules for Building Full Software
By including @heyputer/puter.js in your project, you unlock these key functional modules to handle the entire application lifecycle: 
puter.ai (Intelligence Module): Integrates LLMs like Claude 3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4o, and DeepSeek directly into your app for logic, code generation, or natural language interfaces.
puter.fs (Cloud Filesystem): Replaces the need for a traditional backend file server. It allows your software to read, write, and manage user files directly in the cloud.
puter.kv (Key-Value Database): A simple NoSQL database for storing application state, user preferences, or structured data without setting up a separate database server like MongoDB.
puter.auth (Authentication Module): Handled automatically by Puter. You don't need to write login logic; Puter.js manages user sign-ins and session persistence out of the box.
puter.hosting: Allows you to deploy and host your completed software as a static site or a "Puter App" that runs inside the Puter OS environment. 
How to Include it in Your IDE
Installation: Open your IDE's terminal and run:
npm install @heyputer/puter.js.
Import: In your main JavaScript or TypeScript file, include the library:
javascript
import { puter } from '@heyputer/puter.js';
Use code with caution.

Framework Integration: Puter.js is framework-agnostic and works seamlessly with React, Next.js, Vue, and Angular

### 1. What are Redirects?
In a Single Page Application (SPA) like this, if you were to add navigation (e.g., `vayu.io/project/1`), and a user refreshed the page, the browser would ask Cloudflare for a file at `/project/1/index.html`. Since that file doesn't exist (everything is inside the root `index.html`), the user would get a 404 error. 

The `_redirects` file tells Cloudflare: *"No matter what URL the user types, always serve the main index.html file and let the frontend code handle the routing."*

      <line># @google/genai Coding Guidelines</line>
      <line>This library is sometimes called:</line>
      <line>- Google Gemini API</line>
      <line>- Google GenAI API</line>
      <line>- Google GenAI SDK</line>
      <line>- Gemini API</line>
      <line>- @google/genai</line>
      <line>The Google GenAI SDK can be used to call Gemini models.</line>

      <line>- **Incorrect** `models.create`</line>
      <line>- **Incorrect** `ai.models.create`</line>
      <line>- **Incorrect** `models.getGenerativeModel`</line>
      <line>- **Incorrect** `genAI.getGenerativeModel`</line>

      <line>- **Incorrect** `SchemaType`; **Correct** `Type`.</line>
      <line>When using generate content for text answers, do *not* define the model first and call generate content later. You must use `ai.models.generateContent` to query GenAI with both the model name and prompt.</line>

      <line>- Use this `process.env.API_KEY` string **directly** when initializing the `@google/genai` client instance (must use `new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY })`).</line>
      <line>- Do **not** generate any UI elements (input fields, forms, prompts, configuration sections) or code snippets for entering or managing the API key. Do **not** define `process.env` or request that the user update the API_KEY in the code. The key's availability is handled externally and is a hard requirement. The application **must not** ask the user for it under any circumstances.</line>

      <line>## Model</line>

      <line>  - native audio or gemini flash audio: 'gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025'</line>
      <line>  - gemini tts or gemini text-to-speech: 'gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts'</line>

      <line>  - High-Quality Image Generation and Editing Tasks (supports 1K, 2K, and 4K resolution): 'gemini-3-pro-image-preview'</line>
      <line>  - High-Quality Video Generation Tasks: 'veo-3.1-generate-preview'</line>
      <line>  - General Video Generation Tasks: 'veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview'</line>
      <line>  - Real-time audio & video conversation tasks: 'gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025'</line>

      <line>---</line>
      <line>## Import</line>
      <line>- Always use `import {GoogleGenAI} from "@google/genai";`.</line>
      <line>- **Prohibited:** `import { GoogleGenerativeAI } from "@google/genai";`</line>
      <line>- **Prohibited:** `import type { GoogleGenAI} from "@google/genai";`</line>
      <line>- **Prohibited:** `declare var GoogleGenAI`.</line>
      <line>---</line>
      <line>## Generate Content</line>
      <line>Generate a response from the model.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const response = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-3-flash-preview',</line>
      <line>  contents: 'why is the sky blue?',</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>console.log(response.text);</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>Generate content with multiple parts, for example, by sending an image and a text prompt to the model.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI, GenerateContentResponse } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const imagePart = {</line>
      <line>  inlineData: {</line>
      <line>    mimeType: 'image/png', // Could be any other IANA standard MIME type for the source data.</line>
      <line>    data: base64EncodeString, // base64 encoded string</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>};</line>
      <line>const textPart = {</line>
      <line>  text: promptString // text prompt</line>
      <line>};</line>
      <line>const response: GenerateContentResponse = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-3-flash-preview',</line>
      <line>  contents: { parts: [imagePart, textPart] },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>---</line>
      <line>## Extracting Text Output from `GenerateContentResponse`</line>
      <line>When you use `ai.models.generateContent`, it returns a `GenerateContentResponse` object.</line>
      <line>The simplest and most direct way to get the generated text content is by accessing the `.text` property on this object.</line>
      <line>### Correct Method</line>
      <line>- The `GenerateContentResponse` object features a `text` property (not a method, so do not call `text()`) that directly returns the string output.</line>
      <line>Property definition:</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>export class GenerateContentResponse {</line>
      <line> ......</line>
      <line> get text(): string | undefined {</line>
      <line> // Returns the extracted string output.</line>
      <line> }</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>Example:</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI, GenerateContentResponse } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const response: GenerateContentResponse = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-3-flash-preview',</line>
      <line>  contents: 'why is the sky blue?',</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>const text = response.text; // Do not use response.text()</line>
      <line>console.log(text);</line>
      <line>const chat: Chat = ai.chats.create({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-3-flash-preview',</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>let streamResponse = await chat.sendMessageStream({ message: "Tell me a story in 100 words." });</line>
      <line>for await (const chunk of streamResponse) {</line>
      <line>  const c = chunk as GenerateContentResponse</line>
      <line>  console.log(c.text) // Do not use c.text()</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>### Common Mistakes to Avoid</line>
      <line>- **Incorrect:** `const text = response.text();`</line>
      <line>- **Incorrect:** `const text = response?.response?.text?;`</line>
      <line>- **Incorrect:** `const text = response?.response?.text();`</line>
      <line>- **Incorrect:** `const text = response?.response?.text?.()?.trim();`</line>
      <line>- **Incorrect:** `const json = response.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.[0]?.json;`</line>
      <line>---</line>
      <line>## System Instruction and Other Model Configs</line>
      <line>Generate a response with a system instruction and other model configs.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const response = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>  model: "gemini-3-flash-preview",</line>
      <line>  contents: "Tell me a story.",</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    systemInstruction: "You are a storyteller for kids under 5 years old.",</line>
      <line>    topK: 64,</line>

      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>

      <line>## Max Output Tokens Config</line>
      <line>`maxOutputTokens`: An optional config. It controls the maximum number of tokens the model can utilize for the request.</line>
      <line>- Recommendation: Avoid setting this if not required to prevent the response from being blocked due to reaching max tokens.</line>
      <line>- If you need to set it, you must set a smaller `thinkingBudget` to reserve tokens for the final output.</line>
      <line>**Correct Example for Setting `maxOutputTokens` and `thinkingBudget` Together**</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const response = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>  model: "gemini-3-flash-preview",</line>
      <line>  contents: "Tell me a story.",</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    // The effective token limit for the response is `maxOutputTokens` minus the `thinkingBudget`.</line>

      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>console.log(response.text);</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>**Incorrect Example for Setting `maxOutputTokens` without `thinkingBudget`**</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>

      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>

      <line>  OBJECT = 'OBJECT',</line>

      <line>   * Null type</line>
      <line>   */</line>
      <line>  NULL = 'NULL',</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>Rules:</line>
      <line>* Type.OBJECT cannot be empty; it must contain other properties.</line>
      <line>* Do not use `SchemaType`, it is not available from `@google/genai`</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI, Type } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const response = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>   model: "gemini-3-flash-preview",</line>
      <line>   contents: "List a few popular cookie recipes, and include the amounts of ingredients.",</line>
      <line>   config: {</line>
      <line>     responseMimeType: "application/json",</line>
      <line>     responseSchema: {</line>
      <line>        type: Type.ARRAY, line: items: {</line>
      <line>          type: Type.OBJECT, line: properties: {</line>
      <line>            recipeName: {</line>
      <line>              type: Type.STRING,</line>
      <line>              description: 'The name of the recipe.',</line>
      <line>            },</line>
      <line>            ingredients: {</line>
      <line>              type: Type.ARRAY, line: items: {</line>
      <line>                type: Type.STRING,</line>
      <line>              },</line>
      <line>              description: 'The ingredients for the recipe.',</line>
      <line>            },</line>
      <line>          },</line>
      <line>          propertyOrdering: ["recipeName", "ingredients"],</line>
      <line>        },</line>
      <line>      },</line>
      <line>   },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>let jsonStr = response.text.trim();</line>

      <line>## Function calling</line>
      <line>To let Gemini to interact with external systems, you can provide `FunctionDeclaration` object as `tools`. The model can then return a structured `FunctionCall` object, asking you to call the function with the provided arguments.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { FunctionDeclaration,  GoogleGenAI, Type } from '@google/genai';</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>// Assuming you have defined a function `controlLight` which takes `brightness` and `colorTemperature` as input arguments.</line>
      <line>const controlLightFunctionDeclaration: FunctionDeclaration = {</line>
      <line>  name: 'controlLight',</line>
      <line>  parameters: {</line>
      <line>    type: Type.OBJECT,</line>
      <line>    description: 'Set the brightness and color temperature of a room light.',</line>
      <line>    properties: {</line>
      <line>      brightness: {</line>
      <line>        type: Type.NUMBER,</line>
      <line>        description:</line>
      <line>          'Light level from 0 to 100. Zero is off and 100 is full brightness.',</line>
      <line>      },</line>
      <line>      colorTemperature: {</line>
      <line>        type: Type.STRING,</line>
      <line>        description:</line>
      <line>          'Color temperature of the light fixture such as `daylight`, `cool` or `warm`.',</line>
      <line>      },</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    required: ['brightness', 'colorTemperature'],</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>};</line>
      <line>const response = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-3-flash-preview',</line>
      <line>  contents: 'Dim the lights so the room feels cozy and warm.',</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    tools: [{functionDeclarations: [controlLightFunctionDeclaration]}], // You can pass multiple functions to the model.</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>console.debug(response.functionCalls);</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>the `response.functionCalls` might look like this:</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>[</line>
      <line>  {</line>
      <line>    args: { colorTemperature: 'warm', brightness: 25 },</line>
      <line>    name: 'controlLight',</line>
      <line>    id: 'functionCall-id-123',</line>
      <line>  }</line>
      <line>]</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>You can then extract the arguments from the `FunctionCall` object and execute your `controlLight` function.</line>

      <line>## Generate Images</line>
      <line>### Image Generation/Editing Model</line>
      <line>- Generate images using `gemini-2.5-flash-image` by default; switch to Imagen models (e.g., `imagen-4.0-generate-001`) only if the user explicitly requests them.</line>
      <line>- Upgrade to `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` if the user requests high-quality images (e.g., 2K or 4K resolution).</line>
      <line>- Upgrade to `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` if the user requests real-time information using the `googleSearch` tool.</line>
      <line>  The tool is only available to `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`, do not use it for `gemini-2.5-flash-image`</line>
      <line>- When using `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`, users **MUST** select their own API key.</line>
      <line>  This step is mandatory before accessing the main app.</line>
      <line>  Follow the instructions in the below "API Key Selection" section (identical to the Veo video generation process).</line>
      <line>### Image Configuration</line>
      <line>- `aspectRatio`: Changes the aspect ratio of the generated image. Supported values are "1:1", "3:4", "4:3", "9:16", and "16:9". The default is "1:1".</line>
      <line>- `imageSize`: Changes the size of the generated image. This option is only available for `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`. Supported values are "1K", "2K", and "4K". The default is "1K".</line>
      <line>- **DO NOT** set `responseMimeType`. It is not supported for nano banana series models.</line>
      <line>- **DO NOT** set `responseSchema`. It is not supported for nano banana series models.</line>
      <line>### Examples</line>
      <line>- Call `generateContent` to generate images with nano banana series models; do not use it for Imagen models.</line>
      <line>- The output response may contain both image and text parts; you must iterate through all parts to find the image part. Do not assume the first part is an image part.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const response = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-3-pro-image-preview',</line>
      <line>  contents: {</line>
      <line>    parts: [</line>
      <line>      {</line>
      <line>        text: 'A robot holding a red skateboard.',</line>
      <line>      },</line>
      <line>    ],</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    imageConfig: {</line>
      <line>          aspectRatio: "1:1", line:           imageSize: "1K"</line>
      <line>      },</line>
      <line>    tools: [{google_search: {}}], // Optional, only available for `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`.</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>for (const part of response.candidates[0].content.parts) {</line>
      <line>  // Find the image part, do not assume it is the first part.</line>
      <line>  if (part.inlineData) {</line>
      <line>    const base64EncodeString: string = part.inlineData.data;</line>
      <line>    const imageUrl = `data:image/png;base64,${base64EncodeString}`;</line>
      <line>  } else if (part.text) {</line>
      <line>    console.log(part.text);</line>
      <line>  }</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>- Call `generateImages` to generate images with Imagen models; do not use it for nano banana series models.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const response = await ai.models.generateImages({</line>
      <line>    model: 'imagen-4.0-generate-001',</line>
      <line>    prompt: 'A robot holding a red skateboard.',</line>
      <line>    config: {</line>
      <line>      numberOfImages: 1,</line>
      <line>      outputMimeType: 'image/jpeg',</line>
      <line>      aspectRatio: '1:1',</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>const base64EncodeString: string = response.generatedImages[0].image.imageBytes;</line>
      <line>const imageUrl = `data:image/png;base64,${base64EncodeString}`;</line>
      <line>```</line>

      <line>## Generate Speech</line>
      <line>Transform text input into single-speaker or multi-speaker audio.</line>
      <line>### Single speaker</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI, Modality } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({});</line>
      <line>const response = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>  model: "gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts",</line>
      <line>  contents: [{ parts: [{ text: 'Say cheerfully: Have a wonderful day!' }] }],</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    responseModalities: [Modality.AUDIO], // Must be an array with a single `Modality.AUDIO` element.</line>
      <line>    speechConfig: {</line>
      <line>        voiceConfig: {</line>
      <line>          prebuiltVoiceConfig: { voiceName: 'Kore' },</line>
      <line>        },</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>const outputAudioContext = new (window.AudioContext ||</line>
      <line>  window.webkitAudioContext)({sampleRate: 24000});</line>
      <line>const outputNode = outputAudioContext.createGain();</line>
      <line>const base64Audio = response.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.[0]?.inlineData?.data;</line>
      <line>const audioBuffer = await decodeAudioData(</line>
      <line>  decode(base64EncodedAudioString),</line>
      <line>  outputAudioContext,</line>
      <line>  24000,</line>
      <line>  1,</line>
      <line>);</line>
      <line>const source = outputAudioContext.createBufferSource();</line>
      <line>source.buffer = audioBuffer;</line>
      <line>source.connect(outputNode);</line>
      <line>source.start();</line>
      <line>```</line>

      <line>      Jane: Not too bad, how about you?`;</line>

      <line>                {</line>

      <line>                    voiceConfig: {</line>
      <line>                      prebuiltVoiceConfig: { voiceName: 'Kore' }</line>
      <line>                    }</line>
      <line>                },</line>
      <line>                {</line>
      <line>                    speaker: 'Jane',</line>
      <line>                    voiceConfig: {</line>
      <line>                      prebuiltVoiceConfig: { voiceName: 'Puck' }</line>
      <line>                    }</line>
      <line>                }</line>
      <line>          ]</line>
      <line>        }</line>
      <line>    }</line>
      <line>  }</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>const outputAudioContext = new (window.AudioContext ||</line>
      <line>  window.webkitAudioContext)({sampleRate: 24000});</line>
      <line>const base64Audio = response.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.[0]?.inlineData?.data;</line>
      <line>const audioBuffer = await decodeAudioData(</line>
      <line>  decode(base64EncodedAudioString),</line>
      <line>  outputAudioContext,</line>
      <line>  24000,</line>
      <line>  1,</line>
      <line>);</line>
      <line>const source = outputAudioContext.createBufferSource();</line>
      <line>source.buffer = audioBuffer;</line>
      <line>source.connect(outputNode);</line>
      <line>source.start();</line>

      <line>### Audio Decoding</line>
      <line>* Follow the existing example code from Live API `Audio Encoding & Decoding` section.</line>
      <line>* The audio bytes returned by the API is raw PCM data. It is not a standard file format like `.wav` `.mpeg`, or `.mp3`, it contains no header information.</line>

      <line>## Generate Videos</line>

      <line>The aspect ratio can be `16:9` (landscape) or `9:16` (portrait), the resolution can be 720p or 1080p, and the number of videos must be 1.</line>
      <line>Note: The video generation can take a few minutes. Create a set of clear and reassuring messages to display on the loading screen to improve the user experience.</line>

      <line>### API Key Selection</line>
      <line>When using the Veo video generation models, users must select their own paid API key. This is a mandatory step before accessing the main app.</line>
      <line>Use `await window.aistudio.hasSelectedApiKey()` to check whether an API key has been selected.</line>
      <line>If not, add a button which calls `await window.aistudio.openSelectKey()` to open a dialog for the user to select their API key.</line>
      <line>Assume `window.aistudio.hasSelectedApiKey()` and `window.aistudio.openSelectKey()` are pre-configured, valid, and accessible in the execution context.</line>
      <line>Race condition:</line>
      <line>* A race condition can occur where `hasSelectedApiKey()` may not immediately return true after the user selects a key with `openSelectKey()`. To mitigate this, you MUST assume the key selection was successful after triggering `openSelectKey()` and proceed to the app. Do not add delay to mitigate the race condition.</line>
      <line>* If the request fails with an error message containing "Requested entity was not found.", reset the key selection state and prompt the user to select a key again via `openSelectKey()`.</line>
      <line>* Create a new `GoogleGenAI` instance right before making an API call to ensure it always uses the most up-to-date API key from the dialog. Do not create `GoogleGenAI` when the component is first rendered.</line>
      <line>Important:</line>
      <line>* A link to the billing documentation (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing) must be provided in the dialog. Users must select a API key from a paid GCP project.</line>
      <line>* The selected API key is available via `process.env.API_KEY`. It is injected automatically, so you do not need to modify the API key code.</line>
      <line>---</line>
      <line>## Live</line>
      <line>The Live API enables low-latency, real-time voice interactions with Gemini.</line>
      <line>It can process continuous streams of audio or video input and returns human-like spoken</line>
      <line>audio responses from the model, creating a natural conversational experience.</line>
      <line>This API is primarily designed for audio-in (which can be supplemented with image frames) and audio-out conversations.</line>
      <line>### Session Setup</line>
      <line>Example code for session setup and audio streaming.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import {GoogleGenAI, LiveServerMessage, Modality, Blob} from '@google/genai';</line>
      <line>// The `nextStartTime` variable acts as a cursor to track the end of the audio playback queue.</line>
      <line>// Scheduling each new audio chunk to start at this time ensures smooth, gapless playback.</line>
      <line>let nextStartTime = 0;</line>
      <line>const inputAudioContext = new (window.AudioContext ||</line>
      <line>  window.webkitAudioContext)({sampleRate: 16000});</line>
      <line>const outputAudioContext = new (window.AudioContext ||</line>
      <line>  window.webkitAudioContext)({sampleRate: 24000});</line>
      <line>const inputNode = inputAudioContext.createGain();</line>
      <line>const outputNode = outputAudioContext.createGain();</line>
      <line>const sources = new Set<AudioBufferSourceNode>();</line>
      <line>const stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true });</line>
      <line>const sessionPromise = ai.live.connect({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025',</line>
      <line>  // You must provide callbacks for onopen, onmessage, onerror, and onclose.</line>
      <line>  callbacks: {</line>
      <line>    onopen: () => {</line>
      <line>      // Stream audio from the microphone to the model.</line>
      <line>      const source = inputAudioContext.createMediaStreamSource(stream);</line>
      <line>      const scriptProcessor = inputAudioContext.createScriptProcessor(4096, 1, 1);</line>
      <line>      scriptProcessor.onaudioprocess = (audioProcessingEvent) => {</line>
      <line>        const inputData = audioProcessingEvent.inputBuffer.getChannelData(0);</line>
      <line>        const pcmBlob = createBlob(inputData);</line>
      <line>        // CRITICAL: Solely rely on sessionPromise resolves and then call `session.sendRealtimeInput`, **do not** add other condition checks.</line>
      <line>        sessionPromise.then((session) => {</line>
      <line>          session.sendRealtimeInput({ media: pcmBlob });</line>
      <line>        });</line>
      <line>      };</line>
      <line>      source.connect(scriptProcessor);</line>
      <line>      scriptProcessor.connect(inputAudioContext.destination);</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    onmessage: async (message: LiveServerMessage) => {</line>
      <line>      // Example code to process the model's output audio bytes.</line>
      <line>      // The `LiveServerMessage` only contains the model's turn, not the user's turn.</line>
      <line>      const base64EncodedAudioString =</line>
      <line>        message.serverContent?.modelTurn?.parts[0]?.inlineData.data;</line>
      <line>      if (base64EncodedAudioString) {</line>
      <line>        nextStartTime = Math.max(</line>
      <line>          nextStartTime,</line>
      <line>          outputAudioContext.currentTime,</line>
      <line>        );</line>
      <line>        const audioBuffer = await decodeAudioData(</line>
      <line>          decode(base64EncodedAudioString),</line>
      <line>          outputAudioContext,</line>
      <line>          24000,</line>
      <line>          1,</line>
      <line>        );</line>
      <line>        const source = outputAudioContext.createBufferSource();</line>
      <line>        source.buffer = audioBuffer;</line>
      <line>        source.connect(outputNode);</line>
      <line>        source.addEventListener('ended', () => {</line>
      <line>          sources.delete(source);</line>
      <line>        });</line>
      <line>        source.start(nextStartTime);</line>
      <line>        nextStartTime = nextStartTime + audioBuffer.duration;</line>
      <line>        sources.add(source);</line>
      <line>      }</line>
      <line>      const interrupted = message.serverContent?.interrupted;</line>
      <line>      if (interrupted) {</line>
      <line>        for (const source of sources.values()) {</line>
      <line>          source.stop();</line>
      <line>          sources.delete(source);</line>
      <line>        }</line>
      <line>        nextStartTime = 0;</line>
      <line>      }</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    onerror: (e: ErrorEvent) => {</line>
      <line>      console.debug('got error');</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    onclose: (e: CloseEvent) => {</line>
      <line>      console.debug('closed');</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    responseModalities: [Modality.AUDIO], // Must be an array with a single `Modality.AUDIO` element.</line>
      <line>    speechConfig: {</line>
      <line>      // Other available voice names are `Puck`, `Charon`, `Kore`, and `Fenrir`.</line>
      <line>      voiceConfig: {prebuiltVoiceConfig: {voiceName: 'Zephyr'}},</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    systemInstruction: 'You are a friendly and helpful customer support agent.',</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>function createBlob(data: Float32Array): Blob {</line>
      <line>  const l = data.length;</line>
      <line>  const int16 = new Int16Array(l);</line>
      <line>  for (let i = 0; i < l; i++) {</line>
      <line>    int16[i] = data[i] * 32768;</line>
      <line>  }</line>
      <line>  return {</line>
      <line>    data: encode(new Uint8Array(int16.buffer)),</line>
      <line>    // The supported audio MIME type is 'audio/pcm'. Do not use other types.</line>
      <line>    mimeType: 'audio/pcm;rate=16000',</line>
      <line>  };</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>### Video Streaming</line>
      <line>The model does not directly support video MIME types. To simulate video, you must stream image frames and audio data as separate inputs.</line>
      <line>The following code provides an example of sending image frames to the model.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>const canvasEl: HTMLCanvasElement = /* ... your source canvas element ... */;</line>
      <line>const videoEl: HTMLVideoElement = /* ... your source video element ... */;</line>
      <line>const ctx = canvasEl.getContext('2d');</line>
      <line>frameIntervalRef.current = window.setInterval(() => {</line>
      <line>  canvasEl.width = videoEl.videoWidth;</line>
      <line>  canvasEl.height = videoEl.videoHeight;</line>
      <line>  ctx.drawImage(videoEl, 0, 0, videoEl.videoWidth, videoEl.videoHeight);</line>
      <line>  canvasEl.toBlob(</line>
      <line>      async (blob) => {</line>
      <line>          if (blob) {</line>
      <line>              const base64Data = await blobToBase64(blob);</line>
      <line>              // NOTE: This is important to ensure data is streamed only after the session promise resolves.</line>
      <line>              sessionPromise.then((session) => {</line>
      <line>                session.sendRealtimeInput({</line>
      <line>                  media: { data: base64Data, mimeType: 'image/jpeg' }</line>
      <line>                });</line>
      <line>              });</line>
      <line>          }</line>
      <line>      },</line>
      <line>      'image/jpeg',</line>
      <line>      JPEG_QUALITY</line>
      <line>  );</line>
      <line>}, 1000 / FRAME_RATE);</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>### Audio Encoding & Decoding</line>
      <line>Example Decode Functions:</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>function decode(base64: string) {</line>
      <line>  const binaryString = atob(base64);</line>
      <line>  const len = binaryString.length;</line>
      <line>  const bytes = new Uint8Array(len);</line>
      <line>  for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) {</line>
      <line>    bytes[i] = binaryString.charCodeAt(i);</line>
      <line>  }</line>
      <line>  return bytes;</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>async function decodeAudioData(</line>
      <line>  data: Uint8Array,</line>
      <line>  ctx: AudioContext,</line>
      <line>  sampleRate: number,</line>
      <line>  numChannels: number,</line>
      <line>): Promise<AudioBuffer> {</line>
      <line>  const dataInt16 = new Int16Array(data.buffer);</line>
      <line>  const frameCount = dataInt16.length / numChannels;</line>
      <line>  const buffer = ctx.createBuffer(numChannels, frameCount, sampleRate);</line>
      <line>  for (let channel = 0; channel < numChannels; channel++) {</line>
      <line>    const channelData = buffer.getChannelData(channel);</line>
      <line>    for (let i = 0; i < frameCount; i++) {</line>
      <line>      channelData[i] = dataInt16[i * numChannels + channel] / 32768.0;</line>
      <line>    }</line>
      <line>  }</line>
      <line>  return buffer;</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>Example Encode Functions:</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>function encode(bytes: Uint8Array) {</line>
      <line>  let binary = '';</line>
      <line>  const len = bytes.byteLength;</line>
      <line>  for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) {</line>
      <line>    binary += String.fromCharCode(bytes[i]);</line>
      <line>  }</line>
      <line>  return btoa(binary);</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>### Audio Transcription</line>
      <line>You can enable transcription of the model's audio output by setting `outputAudioTranscription: {}` in the config.</line>
      <line>You can enable transcription of user audio input by setting `inputAudioTranscription: {}` in the config.</line>
      <line>Example Audio Transcription Code:</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import {GoogleGenAI, LiveServerMessage, Modality} from '@google/genai';</line>
      <line>let currentInputTranscription = '';</line>
      <line>let currentOutputTranscription = '';</line>
      <line>const transcriptionHistory = [];</line>
      <line>const sessionPromise = ai.live.connect({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025',</line>
      <line>  callbacks: {</line>
      <line>    onopen: () => {</line>
      <line>      console.debug('opened');</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    onmessage: async (message: LiveServerMessage) => {</line>
      <line>      if (message.serverContent?.outputTranscription) {</line>
      <line>        const text = message.serverContent.outputTranscription.text;</line>
      <line>        currentOutputTranscription += text;</line>
      <line>      } else if (message.serverContent?.inputTranscription) {</line>
      <line>        const text = message.serverContent.inputTranscription.text;</line>
      <line>        currentInputTranscription += text;</line>
      <line>      }</line>
      <line>      // A turn includes a user input and a model output.</line>
      <line>      if (message.serverContent?.turnComplete) {</line>
      <line>        // You can also stream the transcription text as it arrives (before `turnComplete` line:         // to provide a smoother user experience.</line>
      <line>        const fullInputTranscription = currentInputTranscription;</line>
      <line>        const fullOutputTranscription = currentOutputTranscription;</line>
      <line>        console.debug('user input: ', fullInputTranscription);</line>
      <line>        console.debug('model output: ', fullOutputTranscription);</line>
      <line>        transcriptionHistory.push(fullInputTranscription);</line>
      <line>        transcriptionHistory.push(fullOutputTranscription);</line>
      <line>        // IMPORTANT: If you store the transcription in a mutable reference (like React's `useRef` line:         // copy its value to a local variable before clearing it to avoid issues with asynchronous updates.</line>
      <line>        currentInputTranscription = '';</line>
      <line>        currentOutputTranscription = '';</line>
      <line>      }</line>
      <line>      // IMPORTANT: You must still handle the audio output.</line>
      <line>      const base64EncodedAudioString =</line>
      <line>        message.serverContent?.modelTurn?.parts[0]?.inlineData.data;</line>
      <line>      if (base64EncodedAudioString) {</line>
      <line>        /* ... process the audio output (see Session Setup example) ... */</line>
      <line>      }</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    onerror: (e: ErrorEvent) => {</line>
      <line>      console.debug('got error');</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    onclose: (e: CloseEvent) => {</line>
      <line>      console.debug('closed');</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    responseModalities: [Modality.AUDIO], // Must be an array with a single `Modality.AUDIO` element.</line>
      <line>    outputAudioTranscription: {}, // Enable transcription for model output audio.</line>
      <line>    inputAudioTranscription: {}, // Enable transcription for user input audio.</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>### Function Calling</line>
      <line>Live API supports function calling, similar to the `generateContent` request.</line>
      <line>Example Function Calling Code:</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { FunctionDeclaration,  GoogleGenAI, LiveServerMessage, Modality, Type } from '@google/genai';</line>
      <line>// Assuming you have defined a function `controlLight` which takes `brightness` and `colorTemperature` as input arguments.</line>
      <line>const controlLightFunctionDeclaration: FunctionDeclaration = {</line>
      <line>  name: 'controlLight',</line>
      <line>  parameters: {</line>
      <line>    type: Type.OBJECT,</line>
      <line>    description: 'Set the brightness and color temperature of a room light.',</line>
      <line>    properties: {</line>
      <line>      brightness: {</line>
      <line>        type: Type.NUMBER,</line>
      <line>        description:</line>
      <line>          'Light level from 0 to 100. Zero is off and 100 is full brightness.',</line>
      <line>      },</line>
      <line>      colorTemperature: {</line>
      <line>        type: Type.STRING,</line>
      <line>        description:</line>
      <line>          'Color temperature of the light fixture such as `daylight`, `cool` or `warm`.',</line>
      <line>      },</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    required: ['brightness', 'colorTemperature'],</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>};</line>
      <line>const sessionPromise = ai.live.connect({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025',</line>
      <line>  callbacks: {</line>
      <line>    onopen: () => {</line>
      <line>      console.debug('opened');</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    onmessage: async (message: LiveServerMessage) => {</line>
      <line>      if (message.toolCall) {</line>
      <line>        for (const fc of message.toolCall.functionCalls) {</line>
      <line>          /**</line>
      <line>           * The function call might look like this:</line>
      <line>           * {</line>
      <line>           *   args: { colorTemperature: 'warm', brightness: 25 },</line>
      <line>           *   name: 'controlLight',</line>
      <line>           *   id: 'functionCall-id-123',</line>
      <line>           * }</line>
      <line>           */</line>
      <line>          console.debug('function call: ', fc);</line>
      <line>          // Assume you have executed your function:</line>
      <line>          // const result = await controlLight(fc.args.brightness, fc.args.colorTemperature);</line>
      <line>          // After executing the function call, you must send the response back to the model to update the context.</line>
      <line>          const result = "ok"; // Return a simple confirmation to inform the model that the function was executed.</line>
      <line>          sessionPromise.then((session) => {</line>
      <line>            session.sendToolResponse({</line>
      <line>              functionResponses: {</line>
      <line>                id : fc.id, line:                 name: fc.name, line:                 response: { result: result },</line>
      <line>              }</line>
      <line>            })</line>
      <line>          });</line>
      <line>        }</line>
      <line>      }</line>
      <line>      // IMPORTANT: The model might send audio *along with* or *instead of* a tool call.</line>
      <line>      // Always handle the audio stream.</line>
      <line>      const base64EncodedAudioString =</line>
      <line>      message.serverContent?.modelTurn?.parts[0]?.inlineData.data;</line>
      <line>      if (base64EncodedAudioString) {</line>
      <line>        /* ... process the audio output (see Session Setup example) ... */</line>
      <line>      }</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    onerror: (e: ErrorEvent) => {</line>
      <line>      console.debug('got error');</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>    onclose: (e: CloseEvent) => {</line>
      <line>      console.debug('closed');</line>
      <line>    },</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    responseModalities: [Modality.AUDIO], // Must be an array with a single `Modality.AUDIO` element.</line>
      <line>    tools: [{functionDeclarations: [controlLightFunctionDeclaration]}], // You can pass multiple functions to the model.</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>### Live API Rules</line>
      <line>* Always schedule the next audio chunk to start at the exact end time of the previous one when playing the audio playback queue using `AudioBufferSourceNode.start`.</line>
      <line>  Use a running timestamp variable (e.g., `nextStartTime`) to track this end time.</line>
      <line>* When the conversation is finished, use `session.close()` to close the connection and release resources.</line>
      <line>* The `responseModalities` values are mutually exclusive. The array MUST contain exactly one modality, which must be `Modality.AUDIO`.</line>
      <line>  **Incorrect Config:** `responseModalities: [Modality.AUDIO, Modality.TEXT]`</line>
      <line>* There is currently no method to check if a session is active, open, or closed. You can assume the session remains active unless an `ErrorEvent` or `CloseEvent` is received.</line>
      <line>* The Gemini Live API sends a stream of raw PCM audio data. **Do not** use the browser's native `AudioContext.decodeAudioData` method,</line>
      <line>  as it is designed for complete audio files (e.g., MP3, WAV), not raw streams. You must implement the decoding logic as shown in the examples.</line>
      <line>* **Do not** use `encode` and `decode` methods from `js-base64` or other external libraries. You must implement these methods manually, following the provided examples.</line>
      <line>* To prevent a race condition between the live session connection and data streaming, you **must** initiate `sendRealtimeInput` after `live.connect` call resolves.</line>
      <line>* To prevent stale closures in callbacks like `ScriptProcessorNode.onaudioprocess` and `window.setInterval`, always use the session promise (for example, `sessionPromise.then(...)`) to send data. This ensures you are referencing the active, resolved session and not a stale variable from an outer scope. Do not use a separate variable to track if the session is active.</line>
      <line>* When streaming video data, you **must** send a synchronized stream of image frames and audio data to create a video conversation.</line>
      <line>* When the configuration includes audio transcription or function calling, you **must** process the audio output from the model in addition to the transcription or function call arguments.</line>
      <line>---</line>
      <line>## Chat</line>
      <line>Starts a chat and sends a message to the model.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI, Chat, GenerateContentResponse } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const chat: Chat = ai.chats.create({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-3-flash-preview',</line>
      <line>  // The config is the same as the models.generateContent config.</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    systemInstruction: 'You are a storyteller for 5-year-old kids.',</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>let response: GenerateContentResponse = await chat.sendMessage({ message: "Tell me a story in 100 words." });</line>
      <line>console.log(response.text);</line>
      <line>response = await chat.sendMessage({ message: "What happened after that?" });</line>
      <line>console.log(response.text);</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>`chat.sendMessage` only accepts the `message` parameter, do not use `contents`.</line>
      <line>---</line>

      <line>Starts a chat, sends a message to the model, and receives a streaming response.</line>
      <line>```ts</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI, Chat } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const chat: Chat = ai.chats.create({</line>
      <line>  model: 'gemini-3-flash-preview',</line>
      <line>  // The config is the same as the models.generateContent config.</line>
      <line>  config: {</line>
      <line>    systemInstruction: 'You are a storyteller for 5-year-old kids.',</line>
      <line>  },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>let response = await chat.sendMessageStream({ message: "Tell me a story in 100 words." });</line>
      <line>for await (const chunk of response) {</line>
      <line>  const c = chunk as GenerateContentResponse</line>
      <line>  console.log(c.text) // Do not use c.text()</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>response = await chat.sendMessageStream({ message: "What happened after that?" });</line>
      <line>for await (const chunk of response) {</line>
      <line>  const c = chunk as GenerateContentResponse</line>
      <line>  console.log(c.text) // Do not use c.text()</line>
      <line>}</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>`chat.sendMessageStream` only accepts the `message` parameter, do not use `contents`.</line>

      <line>## Search Grounding</line>
      <line>Use Google Search grounding for queries that relate to recent events, recent news, or up-to-date or trending information that the user wants from the web. If Google Search is used, you **MUST ALWAYS** extract the URLs from `groundingChunks` and list them on the web app.</line>
      <line>Config rules when using `googleSearch`:</line>
      <line>- Only `tools`: `googleSearch` is permitted. Do not use it with other tools.</line>
      <line>**Correct**</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";</line>
      <line>const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.API_KEY });</line>
      <line>const response = await ai.models.generateContent({</line>
      <line>   model: "gemini-3-flash-preview",</line>
      <line>   contents: "Who individually won the most bronze medals during the Paris Olympics in 2024?",</line>
      <line>   config: {</line>
      <line>     tools: [{googleSearch: {}}],</line>
      <line>   },</line>
      <line>});</line>
      <line>console.log(response.text);</line>
      <line>/* To get website URLs, in the form [{"web": {"uri": "", "title": ""},  ... }] */</line>
      <line>console.log(response.candidates?.[0]?.groundingMetadata?.groundingChunks);</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>The output `response.text` may not be in JSON format; do not attempt to parse it as JSON.</line>
      <line>```</line>
      <line>---</line>
      <line>## Maps Grounding</line>
      <line>Use Google Maps grounding for queries that relate to geography or place information that the user wants. If Google Maps is used, you MUST ALWAYS extract the URLs from groundingChunks and list them on the web app as links. This includes `groundingChunks.maps.uri` and `groundingChunks.maps.placeAnswerSources.reviewSnippets`.</line>
      <line>Config rules when using googleMaps:</line>
      <line>- Maps grounding is only supported in Gemini 2.5 series models.</line>
      <line>- tools: `googleMaps` may be used with `googleSearch`, but not with any other tools.</line>
      <line>- Where relevant, include the user location, e.g. by querying navigator.geolocation in a browser. This is passed in the toolConfig.</line>
      <line>- **DO NOT** set responseMimeType.</line>
      <line>- **DO NOT** set responseSchema.</line>
      <line>**Correct**</line>

### Why this fixes the error:
1. **`allowImportingTsExtensions`**: TypeScript by default doesn't like it when you use `.tsx` in an `import` statement. This flag tells the compiler that it's okay because a bundler (Vite) will handle it.
2. **`moduleResolution: "Bundler"`**: This is the modern standard for Vite projects. it tells TypeScript to resolve modules following the logic used by tools like Vite/Rollup.
3. **Import Map Removal**: In your `index.html`, the `importmap` was pointing to `esm.sh` URLs. In a standard Vite build, you want Vite to use the versions defined in `package.json` to create a single, optimized bundle. This prevents the browser from trying to fetch React twice.
